formationLabel: Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish established in Williamsburg in 1896 · closed in 1981
currentUse: The former St. Mary of the Angels church at 211 South 4th Street, at Roebling Street, survives as El Puente's Williamsburg Leadership Center. El Puente describes the property as its renovated former Catholic church headquarters and community arts center. This building reuse is separate from St. Mary of the Angels parish life, which the Diocese of Brooklyn says ended in 1981.
summary: St. Mary of the Angels was a Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, established in 1896 and distinct from Annunciation and Brooklyn's other Lithuanian parishes. By the early 1960s it remained one of the Lithuanian national parishes of the New York and Brooklyn area and maintained its own choir. The Diocese of Brooklyn records that it closed in 1981 and that its records are held by the diocesan archives. Its former church at 211 South 4th Street survives in converted community use as El Puente's Williamsburg Leadership Center.

institutionLifecycle.formation: The Diocese of Brooklyn Archives dates St. Mary of the Angels in Williamsburg to 1896 and identifies it as having started as a Lithuanian parish. The available sources do not supply the canonical erection decree or the date when the South 4th Street church opened.
institutionLifecycle.institutionalForm: Lithuanian Roman Catholic national parish; distinct from Annunciation of the BVM and every other Brooklyn parish with a Marian dedication.
institutionLifecycle.terminalStatus: Closed in 1981 according to the Diocese of Brooklyn Archives. The exact decree, effective date, final Mass, and disposition of parish assets remain unresolved.
institutionLifecycle.currentVerification: The Diocese of Brooklyn identifies its Archives as records custodian. El Puente currently identifies 211 South 4th Street as its Williamsburg Leadership Center in a renovated former Catholic church building.

historicalNarrative.text: The Diocese of Brooklyn dates St. Mary of the Angels in Williamsburg to 1896 and says it started as a Lithuanian parish. This official entry establishes the institution's formation year, ethnic purpose, and diocesan identity. The available sources do not expose the erection decree or distinguish preliminary organizing from canonical erection within that year.

historicalNarrative.text: St. Mary of the Angels was not Annunciation of the BVM. The diocesan archive list carries the two as separate historic parishes: Annunciation began as a German parish and became Lithuanian by 1914, while St. Mary of the Angels is separately dated to 1896 as Lithuanian from its start. This separate institutional identity also prevents a shared Marian dedication from becoming an unsupported identity or successor join.

sources.locator: Brooklyn Parishes list, separate entries for Annunciation of the BVM and St. Mary of the Angels

historicalNarrative.text: A Lithuanian-American survey published in 1961 names Queen of Angels among five Lithuanian national parishes in the New York and Brooklyn area and notes that it had its own parish choir. That evidence supports continued Lithuanian institutional and cultural life in the mid-twentieth century, without supplying a building chronology or later terminal event.

sources.locator: Michelsonas, Lietuviu Iseivija Amerikoje, printed pp. 333-334, Queen of Angels parish and choir

historicalNarrative.text: The parish church stood at South 4th and Roebling Streets, corresponding to the present 211 South 4th Street address. Field documentation identifies the former St. Mary of the Angels building at that corner, while El Puente's first-party history describes its Williamsburg center as a renovated former Catholic church and gives the same street address. Together these sources establish physical continuity of the church building into its present community use.

historicalNarrative.text: The Diocese of Brooklyn says St. Mary of the Angels closed in 1981 and directs its records to the diocesan Archives. The listing does not characterize the end as a merger or name a canonical successor. The former building later housed El Puente Academy for thirteen years and remains El Puente's Williamsburg Leadership Center, so parish closure, school tenancy, and present community-center use are three separate events.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The official Diocese of Brooklyn chronology establishes 1896 formation and 1981 closure. St. Mary of the Angels remains distinct from Annunciation of the BVM, which the same official list treats as a separate institution with a different origin and records route. A secondary genealogy page's suggestion to contact Annunciation is not used as merger, successor, or custody evidence because the current diocesan directory places St. Mary of the Angels records at the Archives.
gaps: The organizing and canonical erection instruments within 1896; any worship site before South 4th Street; the church's acquisition, construction, alteration, and dedication dates; the exact closure decree and final Mass; disposition of parish assets and Jonynas windows; any cemetery; complete records coverage; and interior preservation in the converted building remain unresolved.
